verdicts.claim: 04.01.01's flagship happy path inherits compensation from the source booking and clears the gate without interaction; 04.01.03 D-17 forbids exactly that, every time.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED verbatim on both sides. 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:103-104 — 'System opens the composer **pre-filled from the show**: date (venue-local, D-10), venue, compensation (inherited from the booking), setlist (from 18)'; :108-109 — 'The compensation gate evaluates synchronously (CX-01), and passes without interaction because the fee came from the booking'; :27 — 'the show already knows the date, venue, fee and setlist'; D-02 at :263 — 'The platform already holds the show, the setlist, the project and the fee.' Directly negated by 04.01.03-compensation-spec-work-guardrails.md:223 D-17 — 'Compensation is never pre-filled from the source booking, even when the post is raised from context (04.01.01 D-02) | Inheriting the fee leaks the fixer's margin to the dep (DT-15)' and its edge case :140 — 'Compensation does not (DT-15) ... | Compensation step is blank and required, every time'. Both are Decisions of record in the same sub-domain with no reconciling marker, and they cannot both hold: one build ships a three-interaction dep call, the other a mandatory six-facet compensation declaration plus the DT-15 privacy leak.

verdicts.claim: 04.01.01 D-13 asserts one alert per subscriber per post ever with publication as sole trigger; 04.02.04 D-12 sets the cap at two and names two non-publication triggers.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED verbatim. 04.01.01:128 — 'The fan-out fires **once per post per subscriber, ever** (D-13)'; :240 — 'Publication is the fan-out's sole trigger, and bump must not re-fire it (D-13) — one alert per post per subscriber, ever'; :198 — 'alerts fanned out once (D-13)'. Against the owning file: 04.02.04-alert-subscriptions-delivery.md:244 D-12 — 'Two alerts per (user, post), lifetime'; :86 — 'Alerts per (user, post) | 2 lifetime (D-12)'; :148 — 'this is the one legal re-alert. Consumes alert 2 of 2 (D-12)'; :149 — deadline escalation 'Consumes alert 2 of 2', which is an alert with no publication event behind it. A hard integer disagreement between two specs of record; the 1-alert reading silently deletes 04.02.04 D-06's deadline promotion and the targeting-widening re-alert.

verdicts.claim: The 25-slot limit is a soft ceiling in Behavior, in the Decisions table and in the domain CX, and a hard refusal in the Edge Cases table.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED verbatim. 04.01.01:45-46 — 'Soft ceiling: **25 slots per post** — past that it is a hiring round'; D-08 at :269 — 'Soft ceiling 25 slots'; opportunities-casting-cx.md:29 — 'the 25-slot soft ceiling routes here'. Against 04.01.01:148 — 'Post needs 30 slots (a festival's whole crew) | **Refused above 25**; routed to the open call shape (04.07)'. Soft and refused cannot both be encoded, and the Decisions table is the tree's stated authority, so the divergence is real. Downgraded from blocking: the impact is one validation rule on a rare shape, the edge-case row supplies the concrete intended behaviour including user copy, and nothing else in the domain depends on the answer — an implementer can proceed either way without inventing further product behaviour. Note the same cross-cut note at 04.01.01:247 drops the word 'soft' entirely ('The 25-slot ceiling routes here'), which is a third framing.

verdicts.claim: 04.01.02's edge-case table calls the invite-vs-eligibility conflict unresolved and shows a pre-send confirmation prompt, while its own Open Questions table records it resolved with inform-after behaviour.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. The quote at 04.01.02-targeting-distribution-controls.md:47 exists ('Unresolved and important. Recommendation carried to Step 5 ... | Poster: "Sam doesn't meet reads notation — invite anyway?"'), but the answer is in the same file and in the owning sibling: Q-01 at :100 — '✅ RESOLVED — yes. An explicit invite waives eligibility; the mismatch is shown to the poster **on the invite** and on the submission', sourced to 04.01.04-eligibility-requirement-criteria.md:102 D-05, a Decision of record. 'Shown to the poster on the invite' is compatible with the row's copy — an informed override surfaced at invite time is exactly what the row's prompt renders — so the claimed prompt-versus-disclosure fork does not survive: 04.01.04:58 gives the poster-side copy ('You invited them, but they don't read charts — invited anyway') and the applicant-side behaviour ('no block, normal submit'), and both files agree the invite wins and the mismatch is never suppressed. What is left is stale framing prose in one cell, not a behavioural divergence.

verdicts.claim: The 'filled elsewhere' prompt's trigger is a per-type fill window with no value anywhere and no tracked question asking for one.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED as downstream tuning rather than missing product behaviour. The quote is accurate — 04.01.01:166 is the only occurrence of 'typical fill window' in the domain (grep over the whole tree returns one hit) — but per-type staleness intervals are already published in the file that owns board lifespan: 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:62-66 gives the freshness intervals explicitly ('48 h for dep/session/function/crew/support, 30 days for member-wanted, never for deadline-bearing types (the deadline *is* the freshness signal)'), and D-05's table at :52-60 gives per-type 'Removed from board' triggers. A prompt fired on a post older than its type's fill window has those numbers to read. The tree's own convention also treats such intervals as tunable rather than vision-locked — 04.01.01 D-13 at :274 states its numbers and then says 'Intervals stated as the senior-dev call; tunable at /create-prd'. The mechanism, the one-tap terminal action, the close-out coupling and the user copy are all fully specified; only a numeric threshold is unstated, and a competent implementer converges on the published per-type intervals.

verdicts.claim: 04.01.01's slot-state table puts a live applicant count on the board listing; 04.02.01 rejects candidate-visible applicant counts on values grounds.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the column is the poster's view, not the candidate's. 04.01.01:187 does read 'Open | Post published, slot unfilled | Board listing accepting submissions; live applicant count', but the very next row (:188) pairs the same count with the poster-only surface — 'Reviewing | First submission on this slot | Applicant count, **triage entry point (04.04.01)**' — and :189 continues in the poster's voice ('remaining applicants to this slot owed a disposition now'). Board rendering is owned by 04.02.01, which decides explicitly and consistently: DT-09 at :202 rejects a candidate-visible counter, and D-04 at :148 scopes counts to 'Your posts' — 'the poster view (04.04.01), not the candidate view'. Rule 3 applies: the answer is carried authoritatively one file over, in the file that owns the surface, and no reasonable implementer publishes a counter the board's own spec refuses twice.

verdicts.claim: The blocked-invitee case is marked pending against a stage that has run and closed, has no owner, and no open question covers it.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — tracked, and behaviourally bounded. 04.01.02:49 reads '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — **a Trust & Safety (24) boundary**', so the marker does name an owner domain even though the stage label is stale (Q-02 at :101 confirms Step 5 'has run and left this open'). The cascade-side behaviour is settled by the analogous rule at :54 — an invitee who becomes unreachable is 'Treated as unavailable at that position: cascade advances to the next name rather than stalling. **No leak of why they dropped**' — and the viewer side is decided outright at 04.02.01:159: 'A post from a user the viewer has blocked | Never renders, in either direction ... Whether the *poster* is told their invite failed is 04.01.02's open question (leaking a block) — the viewer-side exclusion is unconditional'. So the buildable path converges (silent skip, no reason disclosed) and the only genuinely open residual is a disclosure question routed to the domain that owns it. A stale stage name in an otherwise owned marker is a cosmetic tracking defect.

verdicts.claim: Three of this unit's CX synthesis slots are bare pending markers pointed at a closed stage with no owner, and one has no answer anywhere in the tree.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — two of the three are answered in the children, and the third duplicates a separately-upheld finding. Markers verified at 04.02-discovery-matching-alerts-cx.md:104, :143, :146. But CX-03 q5 (replaying suppressed alerts on a freed evening) is fully decided at 04.02.04:137-140 — D-11's replay rule with all three required conditions, a Timely tier cap and the >3 batching rule — and CX-05 q3 (permission intersection) is answered and says so explicitly at 04.02.04:212: 'Answers CX-05's pending permission question from this side: material copy states only the **recipient's own** facts (D-14)'. Rule 3 disposes of both. CX-05 q5 (a material score invalidated after a tier is computed) is partly covered by 04.02.04:243 D-11 ('the push is a pointer, not a copy of the truth ... the landing surface owns fill status') for the already-delivered case, and its undelivered residual is the same gap tracked separately under 04.02.03's Stale state, which is upheld on its own. Nothing distinct survives here.

verdicts.claim: 04.02.03 declares a Stale state whose entire user-visible behaviour is a pending marker aimed at a closed stage, with no owner and no covering question.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED and genuinely unowned. 04.02.03-material-aware-dep-matching.md:64 — 'Stale | Setlist changed post-scoring | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' is the whole cell, and :52 poses the substance unanswered — 'Setlist changes after matching | Score invalidated. Setlists change constantly, often on the day. | `[PENDING ...]` — **re-score, or accept staleness?**'. The stage is closed by this file's own record (Q-03 at :99 — 'Re-pointed from the completed /ideate-discover Step 5'), no owner is named on either row, and Q-01..Q-04 (:97-100) cover the beachhead, arrangement versions, ubiquity and private credits — not staleness. No answer exists elsewhere: a setlist is not a terms field under 04.01.01 D-09's enumerated terms set (:270), so the post-side rule makes a setlist edit a silent non-terms change and says nothing about rescoring; 04.02.01 D-14's session-stable ranking governs the board, not the cascade. The consequence is stated in the file itself (:78 — 'confidence order *is* the cascade order'), so re-scoring or not changes who is asked first.

verdicts.claim: The candidacy is keyed on role in 04.03.01 and on slot in 04.01.01/04.05.01; because one post can carry two slots with the same role, the keys are not interchangeable.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the premise fails on the actual slot model, so the keys coincide. 04.01.01:38-40 gives the slot a count: 'Each **slot** carries a role, a **count**, its own eligibility criteria and its own compensation value'. The Operator example the finding relies on is therefore two slots with two different roles, not two same-role slots — 04.01.01:29 reads '2 riggers + 1 LD for one load-in', which under a counted slot is rigger×2 and LD×1. No text in the domain asserts or exemplifies two slots sharing one role, and every worked case pairs one role per slot: 04.03.01:95 (bass chair / engineer chair), 04.05.01:154 (drums, bass, keys), 04.05.01:155 ('the doubling keys player who also sings'). With role and slot 1:1 inside a post, 04.03.01:195 D-05's '(submitting entity, post, role)' and 04.05.01:241 D-07's 'per submission, per slot' select the same object, and both files agree on the arithmetic — two chairs, two candidacies, two dispositions. 04.03.01 Q-05 (:214) being answerable from 04.01.01 D-08 is at most a stale open question, not a key contradiction.

verdicts.claim: The type-scoped free-text question ceiling names a type absent from the closed taxonomy and leaves five of the twelve real types with no ceiling.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED on both halves. 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:198 D-08 — 'Type-scoped ceiling — 0 for dep-call/urgent types, 1 for session call / crew / member-wanted, 3 for brief / **A&R** / audition / open call, hard platform ceiling 3.' The taxonomy is closed and platform-curated (04.01.01 D-04 at :265) and enumerates exactly twelve rows at :78-89: dep/sub, session call, function/private hire, audition/casting, brief/RFP, crew/technical labour, festival open call, songwriting camp invitation, support slot, member wanted, open-mic/showcase slot, General call. 'A&R' is not among them, so the rule assigns a ceiling to a type that cannot exist. Five real types get no assignment under any grouping: function/private hire, songwriting camp invitation, support slot, open-mic/showcase slot, General call — and function/private hire is the domain's stated clearest displacement target (04.01.01:80, Q-01 at :282). D-08 does not state a default, and no open question tracks the gap (Q-01..Q-08 at :210-217 cover other things). The 'hard platform ceiling 3' bounds the blast radius, which is why this is a warning and not blocking.

verdicts.claim: Blind mode is declared type-scoped but the per-type property table carries no blind-mode column and only one of twelve types is assigned a value.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the discriminating principle plus three worked cases determine the assignments. 04.03.04-blind-review-mode.md:91 D-02 states both the rule and the test: 'Blind mode is **type-scoped** | **Incoherent for dep calls** (the point is who you are and whether you know the set); **coherent for auditions and house/orchestral work**', and :55 supplies the worked negative with its consequence ('Should not be offerable for that type. | Type-scoped availability'). Two worked positives exist: 04.01.01:81 ('Audition / casting call ... may enable blind mode (04.03.04)') and 04.07:43 ('Batch review begins — blind if enabled (04.03.04), **which is coherent here**'). The principle — offerable where the work is judged as a take, refused where identity or presence is the point — resolves the remaining rows the same way for any competent reader (member wanted, function hire, crew, camp invitation and support slot are all identity/presence shapes; dep is settled). The absence of a column in 04.01.01's table is a documentation-shape issue, not a forced product invention.

verdicts.claim: The evidence threshold that waives an audition has no scale, unit or vocabulary — the evidence model it ranges over is an unquantified five-row ordinal list.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the ordinal list *is* the vocabulary, and a poster-set threshold over it is directly expressible. 04.03.02-evidence-backed-application.md:38 introduces the scale explicitly — 'Evidence types, **in descending order of strength**' — and :42-46 enumerates five ordered values (verified credit with attestor; material history; prior collaboration with the poster's network; completed engagement history; self-claimed skills). A threshold over a five-value ordered enum ('waive at material history or better') needs no numeric scale, is settable by a poster, and is showable to the applicant before they spend time, which is exactly what 04.03.03:101 D-02 requires and what its Q-03 resolution at :111 specifies ('a poster-set threshold ... Evidence resolved → threshold met → audition waived or reduced'). Two implementers converge on the same control: a minimum-evidence-tier selector over the published order.

verdicts.claim: Five CX synthesis slots are blank pending markers aimed at a closed stage with no owner, including three on the cross-cut a sibling's resolved question cites as its authority.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the cited authority exists and the blind-side residuals are properly re-pointed. The five bare markers are verified at 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:103, :105, :154, :155, :156, and the stage is closed (04.03.04:66 — 'Re-pointed from the completed /ideate-discover Step 5'). But the alleged circularity does not hold: 04.03.03:111 Q-03 resolves on 'CX-05, synthesis answer 2', and that answer is present and substantive at 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:152-153 — 'Evidence resolved → threshold met → audition waived or reduced. Poster-set thresholds, since the judgement is theirs.' A resolution resting on an answer that exists is not circular because sibling cells are blank. The CX-03 residuals are owned elsewhere with live targets: 04.03.04:54 and :56 route the metadata-strip and notification side-channel questions to /create-prd-security, :52/:65 route un-blinding to Q-02, and :66's Compromised state carries a correctly re-pointed '`[PENDING — /create-prd-security]`'. What remains is a stale stage label on synthesis cells.

verdicts.claim: One edge-case row states the deadline is displayed viewer-timezone-first, its own copy renders poster-timezone-first, and 04.02.01 D-12 fixes the opposite primacy.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED, and the row is internally unbuildable as written. 04.03.01:87 — 'Deadlines are absolute instants displayed in **the viewer's local timezone with the poster's timezone named**. ... | "Closes 00:00 21 Aug BST (that's 19:00 20 Aug your time)."' The prose puts the viewer's zone first; the copy in the same cell leads with BST, the poster's zone, and parenthesises the viewer's. Only one can be implemented. The cross-file conflict is also real: 04.02.01:246 D-12 — 'Dates render in the **opportunity's local timezone**, with the viewer's offset shown when they differ | ... getting this wrong misses gigs', restated as a filter rule at :90. So the board and the submission screen would present one deadline with different leading zones, which is the exact failure D-12's own rationale names.

verdicts.claim: Five decisions and two states across two sub-domains are built on a post field — the decide-by date — that the file owning the post object never defines, and no open question asks for it.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED. A grep for decide-by across the domain returns 17 hits, none of them in any 04.01.* file. Consumers: 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:52, :96, :110, :136, :158 (Dormant — '≥50% of the publish→decide-by window elapsed'), :160 (Abandoned), D-05 at :211, D-06 at :212, and its own alarm at :192 — 'The post's **decide-by date** is the ceiling on every hold's resolve-by (D-05) and the denominator of the `dormant` trigger. **Without a decide-by, D-05's forcing function has no bound.**' Plus 04.04.03:169, 04.05.01:68, :82, :147, :169, D-05 at :239 and Q-02 at :254 ('Proposed default if yes: decide-by + 7 days'), and 04.07:102. 04.01.01 defines no such field: the post's context list is 'type, acting identity, hirer, decider, date, location, compensation policy' (:38), the authoritative terms set adds only 'slot count, compensation, required criteria' (D-09, :270), the taxonomy table's four scoped properties (:76-89) do not include it, and the only expiry rule keys on the event date (:169 — 'Post's date passes while still `published`'). No open question anywhere requests it, in contrast to 04.05.03:260 Q-07, which does track exactly this class of gap and even audits it ('*Status check: 04.01.01 still carries neither field ... so the gap is live*'). An implementer must either invent a new mandatory composer field for all twelve types or silently alias decide-by to the event date — and 04.06:63 gives member-wanted 'no deadline' at all, so the alias fails there. 04.04.01's most important resolved question (D-05) and the domain's cheapest anti-ghosting act (D-06) both rest on it.

verdicts.claim: The offer fuse is poster-chosen in 04.04.03 and platform-set in 04.04.04, has no length, floor or ceiling for the ordinary offer, and its bounding question is closed cascade-only.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED as an unbounded parameter with a closed tracking target, but not as a flat contradiction. Verified: 04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md:246 D-02 ('Offers **expire**') states no duration; D-07 at :251 and :90 make the offer 'irrevocable for its fuse ... a window they chose'; :150 offers the poster 'a shorter fuse' as their only mitigation; and :170 explicitly parks the ceiling elsewhere — 'the *length* of that window is 04.04.04 Q-03, and this file contributes the constraint that bounds it: a poster-set fuse with no ceiling lets a poster impose an unbounded free option on the candidate'. 04.04.04:97 D-05 then answers only its own scope — 'Fuse is platform-set by urgency tier with a ~3-minute floor' — and closes Q-03 at :105, with DT-04 at :76 framing it as the cascade's problem ('resolves Q-03'). Downgraded from blocking because the two rules are differently scoped (cascade rungs versus ordinary offers) and so can both hold; what is genuinely defective is that 04.04.03 routes its own no-ceiling hazard to a question that closed without covering the non-cascade case, leaving the ordinary offer fuse with no default, no floor and no ceiling and nothing tracking it.

verdicts.claim: 04.04.02 permits the poster to signal 'still in consideration' to a shortlisted applicant; 04.04.01 D-06 forbids telling an applicant a state at all, naming that exact signal as a hope-raising rank leak.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED, and the conflict is doubled by 04.04.02's own resolution. 04.04.02-shortlist-multi-reviewer-scoring.md:69 — 'applicants are **not** auto-notified of shortlisting. **The poster may optionally signal "still in consideration."**', and Q-02 at :121 repeats and blesses that sentence while simultaneously asserting 'RESOLVED — no. Applicants are told a date, never a shortlist state.' Against it: 04.04.01:212 D-06 — 'The applicant is told **a date, not a state** ... **Never "you're a maybe"** (raises hope, leaks a rank — the hazard 04.04.02 Q-02 identifies for shortlists)', and 04.04.03:188 — 'a "pending offer" hint **would leak a shortlist rank** (04.04.02 Q-02's hazard)'. 'Still in consideration' is informationally 'you're a maybe', so whether the control exists in the UI is genuinely forked. Tail defect confirmed: 04.05.04:32 carries a `Shortlisted` pipeline state qualified 'If posters tell (**04.04.02 Q-02 — unresolved**)' against a Q-02 that is resolved.

verdicts.claim: The queue collapses a candidate to one card per identity and never addresses the two-candidacy case its siblings require to render as two.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — D-10's collapse is scoped to repeat submissions within one candidacy, not across candidacies. 04.04.01:216 D-10 reads 'One candidate, one card, **regardless of submission count**', and its worked case at :129 is 'One identity submits **50 times**' with the rationale 'The 50 submissions are an artefact, not evidence about the person' — i.e. spam of a single candidacy, which is precisely what 04.03.01:192 D-02 already collapses upstream: 'Resubmission **supersedes** rather than duplicates — **scoped by D-05's key**', that key being (entity, post, role). The domain is slot-primary throughout — 04.01.01:269 D-08 ('the slot is the fillable unit'), 04.01.01:145 (drums applicants dispositioned while bass stays open), 04.05.01:241 D-07 ('per submission, per slot') and :154 (three slots, three independent debts) — so two role candidacies are two cards in two slot queues, exactly as 04.03.01:95 and 04.05.01:155 require. No statement collapses distinct candidacies, and no reasonable implementer derives one from a rule whose stated subject is submission count.

verdicts.claim: 04.04.03 DT-04 characterises 04.01.03 D-05 as carrying a reconfirm-or-auto-withdraw rule, which the decisions owning terms-change semantics reject.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — a prose slip in a non-normative annotation, against a rule stated identically four times. The misdescription is real: 04.04.03:208 DT-04 lists '**versioned downward edits with reconfirm-or-auto-withdraw (D-05)**', while 04.01.03:211 D-05 says the opposite ('**Silence keeps the applicant in the pool** ... Rejected auto-withdrawing on silence: a musician who applied at £200 and never saw the notice should not lose their place'). But nothing consumes the slip. DT-04's own operative consequences are enumerated at :208 and consequence (3) imports only materiality — 'the materiality definition must be **imported verbatim from 04.01.03 D-05**' — which the file's Decisions table encodes correctly at :245 D-01. The authoritative rule is stated four separate times with identical semantics: 04.01.01:270 D-09 ('no auto-withdraw on silence, no silent grandfathering, and no suspend-until-reconfirm ... **single source of terms-change semantics**'), 04.01.03:211 D-05, 04.01.04:103 D-06 and 04.03.01:203 D-13. A descriptive phrase in a hypothesis cell does not override four Decisions of record that all deliberately point at one owner.

verdicts.claim: 04.05.04 permits an applicant to withdraw while an offer is live and records it as a withdrawal; 04.03.01 D-12 scopes withdrawal to pre-offer states and requires that act to be a decline.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED — two Decisions of record on one user action, with divergent reputation arithmetic. 04.05.04-applicant-pipeline-history.md:55 — 'Applicant withdraws while an offer is live | **Allowed** ... **Entry moves to `withdrawn`**; the live offer's fuse is released back to the poster', formalised as D-06 at :98 ('Applicants **can withdraw** ... which **releases a live offer's fuse**'). Against 04.03.01:202 D-12 — '**Withdrawal is scoped to pre-offer states only** ... Once an offer is live the control hands to 04.04.03' — with the edge case spelled out at :100 ('Withdraw after an offer is live | **Not a withdrawal — a decline** (D-12, DT-07)') and DT-07 at :155 ('Withdrawal and decline are different verbs and the state machine conflated them'). The two branches are not cosmetic: 04.05.01:243 D-09 excludes withdrawals 'from the denominator entirely', whereas a decline is a poster-visible answer that falls to #2 (04.04.03:194) and carries the structured reason 04.04.03:255 D-11 calls the market's only signal that a fee is wrong. One action, two reputation results and two different next steps for the shortlist.

verdicts.claim: The disposition vocabulary is presented as complete and contains no value for a candidate declining a live offer, although declining is a first-class act with its own state and reason model.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED. 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:48 heads the table '### Disposition values — **deliberately few**', and the table at :56-62 carries exactly seven: `won`, `not selected`, `filled elsewhere`, `withdrawn by poster`, `withdrawn by applicant`, `expired`, `no-decision`. `expired` is scoped narrowly at :61 — 'The applicant **never answered** an offer within its fuse' — so it cannot absorb an active decline. A grep for 'declin' across 04.05.01, 04.05.02 and 04.05.04 returns one unrelated hit ('the queue declines to fire'). Meanwhile declining is first-class in 04.04.03: the `Declined` state at :194 ('Candidate declines | Falls to #2 (CX-02). Structured reason if given (D-11)') and D-11 at :255. So the act that ends a candidacy most informatively has no value in a vocabulary declared closed, and each available mapping is wrong in a different direction — `withdrawn by applicant` removes it from the response denominator entirely (D-09, :243), `filled elsewhere` credits the poster with answering the person who answered them.

verdicts.claim: The credit trigger's fire time is defined only relative to a scheduled end, which four of the nine handoff rows do not have — including both launch targets.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED on the evidence as quoted. D-16 is accurate (04.05.03-won-opportunity-handoff.md:245 — 'Trigger fires at scheduled-end + 12h — not at 1am load-out'; narrated at :120), but the claim that '04.01.01 D-10 makes exactly those deadline-shaped' is false for half the named rows: 04.01.01:83 gives 'Crew / technical labour | **Venue-local wall-clock**' and :85 gives 'Songwriting camp invitation | **Venue-local wall-clock**' — both presence shapes with a scheduled event and therefore a scheduled end. Only session call (:79) and brief/RFP (:82) are 'Absolute deadline'. For those two the deadline *is* a scheduled instant, so 'scheduled-end + 12h' reads straightforwardly as deadline + 12h, and nothing in the text suggests the alternative the finding posits (waiting on a downstream completion event). With the enumeration wrong and the residual reading convergent, this does not survive verification.

verdicts.claim: opportunities-casting-cx.md contradicts itself on the alert cap inside one cross-cut — one alert ever, and cap 2 lifetime.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED verbatim, twenty lines apart in CX-01, with no marker on either. opportunities-casting-cx.md:44-46 — 'compensation **edits must never re-fire** the alert ... and publication `bump` must not re-fire either — **one alert per post per subscriber, ever**'; :66 — 'Publication is the fan-out's sole trigger; bump and edit are excluded by rule (D-13). Targeting-widening is the only legal cause of a second alert (**cap 2 lifetime per user/post**).' The map row at :19 adds a third framing ('Publication gate is the fan-out's **sole** trigger'), which 04.02.04:149 falsifies by making a deadline escalation an alert with no publication event. Downgraded from blocking and flagged as the same root defect as the 04.01 finding above: the cap is decided unambiguously in the file that owns the alert pipe (04.02.04:244 D-12 — 'Two alerts per (user, post), lifetime'), and a cross-cut synthesis artefact does not override the owning spec — so the fix is editorial here and substantive there.

verdicts.claim: 04.07 specifies 'waitlisted' as a third disposition tier sent to applicants, while its own resolved Q-02 and 04.05.01's closed vocabulary forbid telling an applicant a waitlist state.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED. 04.07-open-calls-festival-showcase-competition.md:35 — 'Outcome | Won / not selected | **Tiered** — accepted, waitlisted, rejected'; :45 — 'Tiered dispositions go out — accepted, waitlisted, rejected. **All of them (04.05.01)**'; :67 — 'Waitlisted | Tier assigned | See Q-02 — the rot state'. The cited authority contradicts the citation: 04.05.01's closed seven-value table (:56-62) has no `waitlisted`, and the file's own Q-02 at :102 resolves the state away — 'a waitlisted act is either a *backup* — which is a shortlist rank (CX-02), not a hold — or a hold carrying a named blocker and a dated resolve-by; and 04.04.01 D-06 tells the applicant **a date, not a state**'. Downgraded from blocking: the resolved question sits in the same file, is unambiguous, and is corroborated by 04.04.01:212 D-06 and by the absence of the value in the disposition table, so the correct build is determinable — what is defective is the stale Behavior/Happy-Path text that still promises a waitlist notice and mis-cites 04.05.01 as its source.

verdicts.claim: The member-wanted lifecycle has three mutually incompatible lifespans: unbounded, a 60-day submission cutoff, and a 90-day board exit.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — three different mechanisms, not three lifespans. 04.06:36 and :63 say the ad has no *deadline field* ('Open-ended; runs for months'; 'Live, open-ended, no deadline'), which is consistent with platform-side expiry rather than opposed to it — 04.02.01:60 states the terminator as 'Poster closes it, **or** 90 days elapse', i.e. the platform closes it, not the poster. The two 04.02.01 rules also compose cleanly: D-06 at :62-66 is **activity-based** ('any post with **no poster activity** for a type-scoped interval — ... 30 days for member-wanted ... At 2× the interval it auto-tombstones'), so a touched ad never reaches the 60-day tombstone, while D-05's 90 days is the absolute cap. The finding's arithmetic also conflates columns: the '14 days' at :60 is the tombstone *visibility* window for a closed listing (:68-70 — 'a filled or closed post stays visible for the window above'), not a lifespan term. Day 75 is determinate under both rules: tombstoned if untouched since day 45, live if not.

verdicts.claim: The domain index's totals disagree with the parent structure map and with the tree on disk, on both leaf-feature count and Deep Think count.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED against disk. opportunities-casting-index.md:46 — '**Totals**: 5 sub-domains · **22 leaf feature files** · **59 Deep Think hypotheses logged**', repeated at Q-01 (:85 — '5 sub-domains, 2 domain-level features, **22 leaf features**'). The parent says otherwise: ../ideation-index.md:121 — '| 04 | Opportunities & Casting | ... | **5 sub-domains + 23 features** |'. Disk truth, counted in the sandbox: 23 leaf feature files (21 under the five sub-domains plus 04.06 and 04.07) and **156** rows matching `^| DT-n |` across them — not 59. The per-child Deep Think column is stale in the same direction in every sub-domain index: 04.01-…-index.md:26 claims '3 hypotheses' for 04.01.01 against 15 on disk; :28 claims 3 for 04.01.03 against 17; 04.02-…-index.md:26 claims 2 for 04.02.01 against 10; :29 claims 3 for 04.02.04 against 10. A downstream stage provisioning from the index under-counts one leaf feature and 97 recorded hypotheses.

verdicts.reason: REFUTED — stale stage labels over substance that is settled or owned. Both markers exist as quoted (04.06:56 for the orphaned post; 04.07:56 for the 23:59 submission) and the stage is closed (04.06:103 Q-04 — 'Re-pointed from /ideate-discover Step 5, **which has run**'). The 04.06 row's substance is routed as an entity-lifecycle boundary wherever the domain meets it: 04.04.03:176 — 'The posting org dissolves mid-fuse — the band splits | The offer's fuse runs to its end ... Who then owes the fee is an **01 entity-lifecycle boundary** this feature cannot assign' — and 04.05.01:240 D-06 carries the same rule for the obligation ('the debt outlives the human's involvement and **follows the entity** (Q-05)').
